models.notes:
- Weights: the BF16 checkpoint `meta-models/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B` (revision 0fb02478), converted to Megatron
  `torch_dist` with miles' `tools/convert_hf_to_torch_dist.py` at commit bfdcff0e. `--hf-checkpoint` is the full
  checkout, whose `config.json` miles' Muse Spark model provider reads; the recipes train the text model only.
- `MODEL_ARGS` come from miles' `scripts/models/muse-spark-full.py` (radixark/miles PR #4111, commit bfdcff0e),
  printed by `miles/utils/external_utils/model_args_utils.py muse-spark-full`; run the command from a miles checkout
  at that commit.
- It trains on its own rows, built with `--loss-mask-type muse_spark` (data/README.md).
- Train-only runs pass `--debug-skip-weight-update`. Without it, miles' sample weight-version check
  (`miles/utils/weight_version.py`) reads an SGLang argument that `--debug-train-only` leaves unset, and the run
  stops before step 0.
- The published `radixark/miles:muse-spark-open` image ships Transformer Engine's PyTorch extension and flash-attn 2
  compiled against an older PyTorch than its 2.14.1, and both fail to import (undefined
  `c10_cuda_check_implementation`). Rebuild them against the installed PyTorch for the GPUs you train on (sm90 for
  H200, sm100 for B200): TE 2.17.0 from its PyPI sdist and flash-attn 2.7.4.post1 from source, with `-std=c++20`
  as the PyTorch 2.14 headers require.
- On B200, use `--attention-backend fused` (cuDNN fused attention). With `flash`, TE 2.17 selects FlashAttention 4
  (flash-attn-4 4.0.0b19 in the image; FlashAttention 3 is Hopper-only), whose sm100 forward calls
  `quack.activation.sub_packed_f32x2`; the image's quack-kernels 0.6.5 lacks it, and the run stops at step 0.
  `auto` reaches FlashAttention 4 too wherever TE prefers it.
- With the EFA plugin installed, set `EP_SUPPRESS_NCCL_CHECK=1`: DeepEP's import-time check counts every loaded
  `libnccl*` file, takes the plugin's libraries for a second NCCL runtime and stops the process.

`MODEL_ARGS` are slime's `scripts/models/qwen3.5-27B.sh`: Qwen3.8-27B has the Qwen3.5-27B architecture. Its
tokenizer adds 7 special tokens and a default system prompt, so it trains on its own rows (data/README.md).

`MODEL_ARGS` are slime's `scripts/models/qwen3.5-27B.sh`: Qwen3.6-27B has the Qwen3.5-27B architecture and the
tokenizer of Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, so it trains on the Qwen3.5 rows.

`MODEL_ARGS` are slime's `scripts/models/qwen3.5-35B-A3B.sh`: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B has the Qwen3.5-35B-A3B architecture and
a byte-identical tokenizer, so it trains on the Qwen3.5 rows.

`MODEL_ARGS` are slime's `scripts/models/qwen3-32B.sh`. It trains on its own rows, built with slime's `qwen3` loss
mask (data/README.md).
Patch slime's `mask_utils.py` with `data/patch_glm5_mask.py` before building the rows.

- Weights: the BF16 checkpoint `zai-org/GLM-4.7-Flash` (revision 7dd20894), converted to Megatron `torch_dist` with
  miles' `tools/convert_hf_to_torch_dist.py` at miles 0.1.0 (commit 78527b91).
- `MODEL_ARGS` come from miles' `scripts/models/glm4.7-flash.py` at commit 78527b91, printed by
  `miles/utils/external_utils/model_args_utils.py glm4.7-flash`; run the command from a miles checkout at that
  commit.
- It trains on its own rows, built with `--loss-mask-type glm5` after `data/patch_glm5_mask.py` (data/README.md).
  Its `tokenizer.json` is GLM-5.2's, but its chat template differs, so the GLM-5.2 rows do not apply.

- Weights: a BF16 cast of `sgl-project/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-FP8` (an FP8 repackaging of `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash`),
  converted to Megatron `torch_dist` with miles v0.1.0.
- `MODEL_ARGS` come from miles' `miles/utils/external_utils/model_args_utils.py deepseek-v4-flash`; run the command
  from a miles checkout.
- Build the rows with `--loss-mask-type deepseek_v4 --trust-remote-code` from a checkout of
  `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash` that carries `encoding/` (data/README.md).
- The router gate and the score-correction bias stay frozen (`--moe-router-freeze-gate
  --freeze-e-score-correction-bias`), as miles' DeepSeek-V4 training requires.
- Keep the kernel caches (`$KERNEL_CACHE`) on shared storage so pipeline stages reuse each other's TileLang and Triton
  compiles; with per-node caches, step 0 compiles stage by stage.

- Weights: the BF16 checkpoint `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-BF16` (revision bf77c317), with no
  conversion: miles loads it through Megatron-Bridge (`--megatron-to-hf-mode bridge`), so `--hf-checkpoint` and
  `--ref-load` are both the checkpoint directory.
- `MODEL_ARGS` come from miles' `scripts/models/nemotron-3-nano-30b-a3b.py` at commit 78527b91, printed by
  `miles/utils/external_utils/model_args_utils.py nemotron-3-nano-30b-a3b`; run the command from a miles checkout
  at that commit.
- It trains on its own rows, built with `--loss-mask-type qwen3_5` (data/README.md).

- Weights: `openai/gpt-oss-120b` (revision b5c939de) with its MXFP4 experts dequantized to BF16 by the training
  image's `tools/preprocess_gpt_oss.py`, converted to Megatron `torch_dist` with slime's
  `tools/convert_hf_to_torch_dist.py`.
- `MODEL_ARGS` are the architecture written out in the command, with `--spec attune_gpt_oss_yarn
  get_gpt_oss_yarn_spec`. The spec in `patches/attune_gpt_oss_yarn.py` sets YaRN RoPE from the checkpoint's
  `config.json`, which slime's stock gpt-oss script does not build.
- It trains on the gpt-oss rows; the tokenizer and chat template are byte-identical to gpt-oss-20b's.

- Weights: `openai/gpt-oss-20b` (revision 6cee5e81) with its MXFP4 experts dequantized to BF16 by the training image's
  `tools/preprocess_gpt_oss.py`, converted to Megatron `torch_dist` with slime's `tools/convert_hf_to_torch_dist.py`.
- `MODEL_ARGS` are the architecture written out in the command, with `--spec attune_gpt_oss_yarn
  get_gpt_oss_yarn_spec`. The spec in `patches/attune_gpt_oss_yarn.py` sets YaRN RoPE from the checkpoint's
  `config.json`, which slime's stock gpt-oss script does not build.
- The loss is the mean over each row's supervised tokens (Megatron-Bridge's SFT loss mode); the command does not pass
  `--calculate-per-token-loss`.
- On 80 GB GPUs the FP32 logits of an 8,192-token microbatch (6.14 GiB) leave no room to keep every layer's
  activations, so H100 recipes recompute layers; H200 and B200 hold them.
